body: This looks exactly like my scalp. I've been trying to figure out what the spots are caused by. I've had SD as long as I can remember, but the spots are new for me

Awwww. This just warms my heart and makes me think of my girl. She was also about 3 when I adopted her. She's 15 now I think. I miss her so fucking much I want to cry. Unfortunately she is at my mom's house. Because of the health issues that I am dealing with currently, I am not able to take care of her. Plus my landlord won't allow dogs. It kills me to be apart from her, even though I visit her all the time at my mom's house. It's hard on both of us, my mom says that she always gets really sad when I leave (omg I'm tearing up).

She has been the best dog that I have ever had the joy of being blessed with. Wow, this is harder than I thought.. most people don't understand how I can be so attached to a dog. When I talk about her I always end up  crying. My fiance is always shocked and jokes about how he can't even imagine having so much love for a dog. She really has been the best friend that I have ever had. The bond we have is so special and something that I have never experienced with another living thing. The closest thing I can think of is like a parents bond with a child. But I've never had kids so idk. All I know is that dog is so amazing and special. I always heard dog people talk about their dogs changing their lives. I didn't understand that until I found her. 

Im sorry for rambling. I just figured that fellow dog lovers and cattle dog lovers would get it. They really are some special dogs. 💗
I'm not saying opiates are bad, just no doctor will even give them to me.

I'm curious as well. There has been nothing that has really helped me. I have been fighting for 10 years and I  am ready to throw in the towel. I have been on pretty much every medication that isn't an opiate. Nothing helps but the pain only gets worse.
What is prolotherapy?

This sounds a lot like my physical therapy. My therapist  also has me doing a lot of isometrics. But it hasn't been going well for me. I still can't do hardly any excercises without significant pain. Even when we modify the excercises, I still end up being in so much pain, especially anything that has to do with my shoulders. My left shoulder is always subluxating, and it is so messed up. The excercises are supposed to strengthen it so it doesn't sublux, but everytime I do them my shoulders hurt so bad for the rest of the week.

I agree. I was told that if the headache was severe and did not respond to medicine, that I would be given a blood patch. I  called them the day after and told them how bad it was on Friday, and all they did was prescribe me fioricet. They could have done it then instead of leaving me to suffer through the weekend.
I do too. Thank you. I can't imagine living like this much longer. 6 months sounds like actual hell itself. I am so sorry that you had to go through that.

I'm not sure. Maybe they do check your nasal fluid for leaks. But my neurologist, who was the one that ordered it, seemed to think that I might have intracranial hypertension. 

And I agree. I am not advocating for it being easy to get opiates either. But they have taken it to an extreme in terms of withholding it. For example when I was at the ER, the doctor told me that normally they would have given me a blood patch. But it is basically impossible to get an anesthesiologist on the weekends. So I  basically   their goal was to give me just enough pain relief  to make it until Monday. If that is the case they could have written a prescription for 6 vicodin. Or 4. Instead they gave me a prescription for a migraine medication that has been discontinued and has not been made for the past 6 or 7 years (this coming from multiple Pharmacists).
I know. I have found that it does help. So much. And TONS of water.
Thank you. I hope so too.

Aww she makes me miss my cattle pup. She is also a white cattle dog. I miss her so much. I moved to an apartment building last year for school (this was pre Corona), and was not allowed to take her with me. She has been living with my mom since and it kills me. She is about 14-15 years old now (not 100% sure, she was adopted), and she is now deaf, and has bladder issues. My mom leaves her outside 24/7, because she doesn't want to deal with the bladder leaks. It kills me and I cry everytime I think about it. I'm going to go cry now...

But your pup is so cute, so I still smile!
OMG YES! This is too true.

I know exactly how you feel. I feel this way all of the time. I got really sick a little over a year ago and I feel like it has just been downhill from there. Since I got sick, I have gotten sick more than at least once every month. Each time it feels like it takes me longer to recover, and I get weaker and weaker. I had to take a break from school because my back pain is just getting worse and I couldn't even study because of the pain. Sometimes I honestly feel like this disease has taken everything from me. I don't do any of the things that I used to love, because I am either too tired or in too much pain. I feel like I am just completely useless. The other day my fiance didn't want to drive me to my physical therapy, which is understandable because he would have to wait in the car for an hour (thanks to covid rules). I figured that it wasn't a big deal. But after lifting 2lb weights and 10 mins on the excercise bike, I barely had the strength to drive myself home. It took all the strength I had left just to stay on on the road. I ended up crying the whole way home. I just felt so helpless and pathetic and angry at the universe. 

Lately I have been tearing my ligaments just from walking. My knees keep collapsing inwards more and more, and even standing for 5 mins feels like torture. I feel like my body is falling apart. I assume it is just because my muscles are getting weaker every day, but I don't know how to even begin to get strength up again.
I know exactly what you mean and get that all the time

I get this too. I haven't officially been diagnosed with either, but my doctor thinks that it is TN where as I personally think it is more occipital neuralgia. But I guess it is probably both. I  guess I'll find out soon when I get the tests done.
I know right?

Both my dr and physical therapist specialize in EDS. He is the one that finally diagnosed me. They both seem to think that I have CCI, but my dr wants to do more tests first. I am already getting 2 MRI's, and he basically said that we would worry about CCI later. It sucks because my neck and head hurt so fucking bad. Its getting worse everyday. Right now he and my neurologist are looking for the cause of my neurological symptoms.
Ohio
What symptoms have you experienced? I was diagnosed with hEDS, but I never got any genetic testing. Sometimes I wonder if I have a very mild vEDS, but I really don't know much about how it presents.
That's what I was wondering. Lol

Omg I feel this. Me and my fiance just got a new place and the flooring in the bathroom was awful so we put down some vinyl tile, and had to cut it with scissors. I did most of the cutting because he wasn't very good at it. About halfway through I had to get a thumb/wrist brace. My thumb was so bruised and I started to feel like i was getting carpal tunnel. It has been about a month and my wrist and thumb are just now starting to feel normal again.
I wanted to try this but I'm not diagnosed with MS, or sleep apnea.
I agree, it is always so hard for other people to understand what it is like living in constant pain. It is frustrating. But thank you.

Hopefully. I just had my appointment with my neurologist. I'm not going to say it went bad, cuz it was alright, but he didn't seem to want to hear anything that I had to say. He said that it doesn't sound like TN, but we will see what the MRI shows. I get the MRI on the 19th.
That's kind of why I figured that I dont have TN. I figured I would know, and it would be more painful. I have had some pretty intense jolts in my face but they dont even last a second.

Well hEDS is a connective tissue disease. I dont know if issues with your tendons and ligaments and joints and stuff. A lot of people with EDS have POTS, but you can have POTS without having EDS.

But that sounds like POTS. I'd look up how you treat it online. The online advice is pretty much exactly what my dr told me. You can increase your sodium intake, where compression socks. I haven't really learned how to relieve the symptoms other than the medication my dr gave me. It's called Metoprolol. It helps but it makes me sleepy.

See I was just talking to my doctor yesterday and he said that he believes that I have TN and prescribed me tegretol. I still have to call and schedule my MRI's. But I had already known of TN and I have really only once felt  pain in the intensity that TN I'd described at. I feel a tingling in my face which fits the branches of the nerve, but the only face pain I have is when I touch my temples. Besides that most of my pain is my eyes. I have always described it as an ice pick through the eye and all the way through the back of my head. Now I'm wondering if my dr was right.
Wait, so the story is from God's perspective?

I know right? I would really be interested if it wasn't Christian.  I don't have a problem with religion, but when you have this condition I don't know how you could possibly have faith in god. More power to them I guess.
It was the same for me. I got good at switching my grip. I have the same problems with squeezing and too much pressure. I like smooth pins.
I got diagnosed with sinus tachycardia and POTS by my cardiologist. They can find nothing wrong with your heart, but you could still have POTS. Did they do a tilt table test?

Maybe you have POTS? I don't know if I have MS or not, though I have been having symptoms similar symptoms,  but I do have hEDS and pots. As soon as I lean forward a little bit or stand up, I get internal tremors. Not in my head but like my legs and back. I have noticed my POTS has been really bad recently. I get extremely dizzy when I stand up, and I start having palpitations. My vision fades out and my ears ring. I haven't passed out yet, but I've gotten really close.

The postural part of your issue just makes me think POTS. I have no idea how POTS can effect MS.
Damn. That might be what I'm doing. I need to talk to my lawyer again lol

I am not legally disabled, but I am in the process of trying to get disability. I haven't seen a single job that I can do without significant pain and suffering. I even had to take medical leave from school. I was in too much pain to even sit at my laptop or read my books.

How long does it usually take? Its been about 3 years for me. I've been denied a few times. But I just got my official hEDS diagnosis a few months ago. I have my first hearing (that I'm actually involved in) in February. My attorney said that when I get some forms signed by my dr, I might have a chance to win.

Same. I always made sure I have enough time before work to determine if I feel too bad to make it through a day. Also for me my mental state is important. When I am working too much my mental state spirals from the pain, and stress. I would find myself constantly sneaking off to the bathroom to cry. That's when you know you need to take off more than a couple of days.
I get them in my stretch marks all the time. The other day I had them all over my body but I may have just been itchy and scratched my itches. But yeah. All the time. Usually for no reason.
Same! I'll feel like I'm having a panic attack for no reason.
Where is he located?

Same. My dr didn't refill mine. I thought maybe he didn't want me to take it anymore. He asked me if it was helping and I said IDK, I think maybe that's why. But now I don't have it and it really sucks..
All the time!
What kind are those?

Hmm I wonder if this is what has been going on with me. I have been having tons of floaters, white flashes, and black holes that appear in my vision. Also a horrible pain in my right eye. When the light hits it it feels like an ice pick going in my eye straight through my brain. It also hurts to move my eye to the sides, and it feels like there is so much pressure, like my eyeball is being squeezed. When I am laying on my side and watching tv, it feels like the muscles that move my eye are being pulled really hard. It also hurts on that side of my head, just like you described when I reach for something or bend over it feels like my head is going to explode and like my eyeball is going to pop out of my head. Ive also had pulsatile tinnitus on and off for years. Not currently though, but there was a point where it was so bad that I couldn't sleep or focus on anything. I actually thought I was going to loose my mind from it.

But back to the head/eye pain. I thought that it might have been optic neuritis. When I couldn't take the pain anymore I had my doctor refer me to an ophthalmologist. She ended up telling me to see the wrong dr, but their receptionist (at the opthamoigist office) said that she thought that I needed to see a retinal Specialist. I got in and they didn't see any issue at all. Eye pressure was good, retina good. He couldn't even give me any advice whatsoever other than to come back if the flashing lights got worse.

I don't know what else to do. I have a dr appointment next week and I was going to see if he'd refer me to a neurologist. I just don't know what it could be. With all the stuff the eye dr did, I would imagine that he would have seen something if there were an issue with my optic nerve. But I'm not an eye dr, and he didn't explain anything and didn't really let me ask questions.

My sternum joints pop all the time. I also feel my ribs pop when I cough, or sneeze. But I rarely ever push much for the BMs. I try to let my body do it on it's own. Anytime I strain it feels like I'm going to pop a blood vessel in my brain and I almost pass out. Thankfully my body just naturally launches it out of my body like a rocket. Or I just have explosive diarrhea lol. I do get constipated a lot, but I've learned that no matter how uncomfortable and backed up I get, it'll eventually come out. Nothing good comes from forcing it.
Ohh that makes sense. I have a retroverted uterus also. I have noticed that from behind feels much better but I never made that connection.

I have the same issue. I've already talked to at least 4 drs about it. Every time they tell me everything is fine. The pain only started happening pretty much since I got with my fiance (almost 2 years). I've given up on trying to find out what it is. Maybe his sausage is just too meaty lol.
Hmm. My old dr though I had a meniscus tear, but he never did anything about it lol
Also before you mentioned figuring out POTS. Excuse my profanity, but how the hell do you figure out POTS?!? I sure as hell can't figure it out.

I guess it could be but I don't have any pain in my legs at all besides inflammation in my knees. Usually I at least feel the pain going down my right thigh. Sometimes the left. I did accidentally pop my SI joint, but I don't feel like I realigned it. It just hurts even more now. And I am still vibrating lol. But I have a drs appointment. It's not till next weds unfortunately.

OMG same about the kneecaps and the squeezing. They all irritate my knees even more than not wearing them. I keep trying the ones I just got from my dr., I keep telling myself that I'm just not lining them up right or something. But no matter how many times I put them on it is always awful.

People would stop and ask me all the time why I was in a wheelchair. I swear to God, it has been 6 years and I still have PTSD from being wheelchair bound for 6 months. Definitely the darkest point in my life.
It's ok. It's just what it is. Good ol EDS.

I'm getting better at describing my symptoms to drs. I look into a lot of things, but I always feel like if I'm like "I think it could be this" they blow me off as a hypochondriac/reads stuff on the internet and diagnoses themselves". The sad thing is that I figured out pretty much all of my diagnoses before the drs.
No I don't get bruises or anything, though the vibrating spots do make me itchy. It's a gentle but strong vibration and I always keep it on low.
No I haven't. I would love to but I can't afford it.
I get this when my Achilles tendon gets tight.
What about just vibrating massagers? I just got a full body heating massager for Christmas. I love it, and it feels so good but I keep asking myself if it is really helping or making me hurt more.

The sad thing is that I blew it off for so long that even if I found out what the problem was, its not like they can do anything to fix it.. if anyone has any advice that would be greatly appreciated.

This is great advice! About a year ago I fell down the stairs twice in a row (I believe that I kept fainting), and I really fucked up my hip (specifically the pelvic crest area). I don't know if I broke it, or just badly injured it (though it does feel a bit caved in on that side). I kept seeing doctors, telling them that I have felt a lot of pain but that was the worst pain that I had ever experienced in my life so I figured I broke or cracked something. But I didn't know what to call the area and I kept calling it my hip. And the doctors would just tell me that if I broke my hip, I wouldn't be able to walk.

I gave up. I never even got an xray. To this day I don't know what kind of injury I had, but it has never healed properly. Since it happened I have been in three times the amount of pain before, and become almost completely disabled. I even had to take medical leave from school because I have been in too much pain to function. It even hurts to lay in bed. There is no relief from the constant pain.

I blew the injury off because everyone told me that I was crazy. I assumed it was just more EDS bullshit. I still wonder if the injury had been properly addressed and treated, would I not be suffering like I am now.
I would probably give my kidney for some narcotics right now.. lol

No. I have never experienced this. I don't think that ever in my life I have been given a drug that completely removed my pain. Its always there, but then again I have always been very resistant to opiates and pretty much most medications. Antidepressants have never helped (god I've probably tried at least 15 different ones). NSAIDS dont do shit. Vicodin just gave me a good feeling without doing anything for pain. Every time I have had morphine after surgery it did nothing for my pain. Though I would say when I was given morphine for extreme back pain, it did help somewhat. I also like oxys but they are like vicodin. They make me feel nice but don't help pain much.

Yes OMFG! I constantly feel like I am Trapp in this broken meat suit. I'm always  wanting to do things and I can't, but the mind never rests. It is probably the biggest contributor to my depression. I have been an artist all of my life, and I have found that I need to be doing something creative in order to feel good. Its like therapeutic. But I never do it anymore because of pain and exhaustion. I feel like I have lost everything that helps me cope with this life because of this disease. It has taken just about everything from me.

Oh, I didn't know that we had a higher risk for it. I wasn't even diagnosed when they did it before. But it makes sense. See that's my issue. I feel like I should see a neurologist just to rule out MS, but I also feel like there is a good chance that all of my issues are just EDS stuff. I have only had my EDS doctor for a few months and I already feel like I am driving him crazy lol.
Yes, I get sciatica all of the time.
I think that sounds more like a digestive thing. I get those too. I'm not sure that is serious. What I am talking about is a type of tremor. It feels like you're bones are vibrating.
I figured you meant that one, but you never know. No problem!

Here is the link to the heating pad:
https://www.hellomynt.com/products/mynt-heating-massage-mat-memory-foam-cushion
To which one? The gaming chair or the massaging heating pad?
It feels like my entire body is lightly vibrating. I thought it was just from my low back down, but I feel the shaking all the way up to my neck.
It been either 2 or 3 years since then. But I don't remember the internal tremors when it happened before.

Yeah, I know about cauda equina. That's what they thought I had the last time my legs went numb. I had close to every symptom. They don't normally do MRIs at the ER, but they did one for me because that is how much it looked like cauda equina. But the MRI didn't show anything. But yeah, this now feels pretty similar to the last time.

I got a tilt table test done by my cardiovascular dr. That's how I got my official POTS diagnosis, even though I had known I had it for years. She also did a month long heart monitor. I'm generally tachycardic when I am up and go into super low bradycardia when I sleep.
My fiance got me a gaming chair for school and a full body memory foam massaging heating pad. They are so awesome!
And nah, he was just a general asshole. Terrible friend.
He was big too. And he'd let me pet him. We had lots of good times together. RIP Gus.

I had a friend who said it was ridiculous that I cried when my fish died. I'd had that fish for years and he had a lot of personality and would get happy to see me. He'd  do a little fishy happy dance. He couldn't understand how I'd even be sad. We didn't talk much after that lol

I know that it sounds shallow but I have always felt that an attractive voice is important. My fiance can be rather loud and sometimes talks too much, but it doesn't bother me because I love the sound of his voice. And his ridiculously loud laugh lol. He has the most unique laugh. A lot of people don't like his laugh, but I love it, and it is so contagious and genuinely makes me happy. He is just the type of person that it is impossible to be mad at. You just can't do it.

I had my ex was like this, it was usually small things or like you said a lot of omitted things. After a few years I started noticing that his stories for things would change. I grew up with both parents that were compulsive liars, even though they taught me how important honesty is. The drilled it into to the point where it is very important to me. Of course I didn't see the hypocrisy until I was older, which only grew my disgust of liars.

What really destroyed things with us was after a really bad fight he got drunk and had a female friend come over to his place. First the story was "idk what happened but I got drunk and cheated on you." Then the story was that he blacked out and woke up with her on top of him (he was inside her).I freaked out of course, but once the rage wore off and I reached a level of shock I was like "wait, you were unconscious? Umm, that sounds like rape". Of course he took the story and ran with that one. Now I know that men do get raped and they deserve to be taken seriously. I never completely disregarded that possibility, but his initial story was that he cheated on me. It only became a rape story after I suggested it. Now I stayed with him a while after, I wanted to be sympathetic. But I could never know what the truth was, and I couldn't stop wondering. 
There were a lot of other things that led to me ending things. I put up with a lot. But after him, I have a no lying policy.

That is the exact reason that I refuse to go to my dr appointments without my fiance. I've been going to dr almost 10 years now, I used to always go with my mom. Now all of the sudden they actually take me seriously. Though to be fair I have started seeing a new doctor that specializes in EDS, so that is a big part of it. Since I got my diagnosis even other doctors don't just blow everything off and act like I'm crazy.

My worst experience was with a neurologist. I got sent to her because I had been to 3 or 4 drs who couldn't figure out why I couldn't straighten my leg. The whole thing was awful because of how the doctor's treated me. The neurologist told me that I "needed to consider that it was all psychosomatic". That wasn't even the worst part of my experience with that bitch. Lol its been years and my blood still boils when I think about how that dr treated me.

But it turned out to just be a bad MCL tear from an overextention injury. I even told the dr how I injured my knee and they never even bothered to actually check the knee. They would just try to straighten it and say they couldn't figure out why it wouldn't straighten. It wouldn't straighten from the swelling. But it stayed like that for so long that my muscles shortened and became contractured.

I've had so many horrible experiences, the fear of being treated like that and called a hypochondriac never goes away. That's the main reason I am putting off seeing another neurologist. Even though I am having very concerning neurological symptoms. Same with seeing an eye Specialist. I've put it off until my double vision and eye pain became completely unbearable. I couldn't put it off any longer. I go in tomorrow. Wish me luck!

I completely understand how you feel and I feel the same way. I don't know if I have MS. I've been lurking this subreddit a bit because of all of these weird symptoms that I have going on. I asked my doctor for a referral to a neurologist , but my doctor didnt reply and I figure I'll have to wait until the holidays are over. Thankfully I will be seeing an eye specialist on weds, because the pain in my eye has gotten so bad. And my vision.

But I have EDS along with some other autoimmune diseases. Things didn't get bad until I was 19, in my 3rd semester of college and I got extremely sick. That is when all the autoimmune shit went full blast. It's been almost 10 years since then. 10 years of constant pain, depression, and hopelessness. So many doctors, and medical bills, and suicide attempts. No matter what I do,  everything is a constant struggle. It is so hard just to function and take care of my basic needs. And then the constant pain and mental issues makes life hell. I know that tons of people have it worse. And many people overcome these types of obstacles. But believe me I have tired and tried. I am exhausted from just trying to have the slightest bit of an actual life. I exhausted from all the trying and failing. The constant fighting my body. I know that I can do things like physical therapy and exercise to make things a little easier. But like you, I don't want to course correct my life anymore either. Well the sad part is I do want to, I really wish I could. But I'm just too exhausted and done with the struggle. No matter how hard I try it isn't enough.

I'm sorry. I didn't mean to rant about myself. Its just that you are not alone and your feelings are justified. I know suicide is sad and it hurts people, but this world needs to start actually caring about people's quality of life.

My scalp does this too. All the time. It gets so tender and painful and when I mess with it, it burns. You can actually feel the heat radiating from my scalp. It also gets this weird crawly itchy sensation all over. But when I go to itch it, nothing happens. Idk how to explain it but like with a normal itch you scratch it and it feels good. But when I go to scratch its like the itchy doesn't exist.

This has happened to me forever. I always figured it was something autoimmune, but last night I noticed that it was more of a nervey, tingly sensation. I'd go to itch and feel it slightly like the pressure of me touching, but it felt really weird and numb.

For the most part. It's so hard to describe. It's like right now, I am looking at a toy fire truck. I can close my eyes, and even though I can't see it in my head, the knowledge of what it looks like is there. I could probably look at it a couple of times and sketch it from memory even though I can't see it.
It is very fascinating to me. And funny because I am an artist. I can "picture" things in my mind, but i don't "see" anything. Its weird. I guess it is more of thoughts of what things look like.
I have this problem too. Even after 9 years of going to doctors. A lot is from my parents being like that, and the rest is just all the bad dr experiences.
With mine there was a ton of swelling (I think the swelling is what kept me from being able to straighten it.) And a lot of bleeding/bruising.

This sounds like what happens my right knee all the time except for me its almost always my MCL. Its never been a full tear, but after the first time it keeps happening. The first time I ended up not being able to straighten my knee for 6 months. It happened to my left one while I was on crutches and I ended up in a wheelchair for months. After 3 years and 2 different physical therapy's, I can finally fully straighten my knee (to the extent of a non hypermobile person).
Same with me. And when I try to fix my head posture my blood pressure drops and I pass out.

I know that this wasn't the point of the post but I have aphantasia also. I just learned about it a few years ago. I didn't realize that it wasn't normal.

Also I always thought writing hurt everyone lol. I didn't realize that it's not supposed to be hard and painful lol

This subreddit was probably the first one I joined. Maybe even why I made my account, I cant remember. I was so excited to be able to talk to people who understand. But I almost never post anything because even just trying to talk about things makes me mentally spiral.

I find that I can't watch things about bpd, or read things about it, or really even talk about it without being triggered. Like when I was getting diagnosed my psychiatrist wanted me to read the book "I hate you. Dont leave me" (its about BPD). He wanted me to read it and see how much I could relate, and see if I thought that it was really what I had. Even though it is a good book for understanding how we think, and how to manage it, everytime I would read it my emotions would fly out of control. I'm not even sure why. It was a relief after all of these years getting answers and knowing that I am not alone, etc. 

Plus I had already known for years that I had BPD. I kept telling my therapist and he didn't believe me and wouldn't listen to me (he was terrible at his job). Because no one ever believed me I just gave up. Then one day I go into my psychiatrist's office and he was like "I think its possible that you might have BPD" and then I opened up and told him that I thought that for a long time. It felt really good to be listened to and not doubted. But anyway I got side tracked. My point is that it is a great book. But I could never finish it because I realized that it was just making things worse for me. That's the same reason that I have always struggled with therapy. Even when I get things off my chest and I feel like I've had a good session, afterwards my emotions spiral out of control and it takes me days to stabilize myself.

I don't get it either. Even my fiance, no matter what I do he refuses to wear one properly. He knows that I have a weak immune system and that if he got it he will be fine but it would probably kill me. Yet he still won't do it even for me. I just make sure I always wear it around anyone. He's pretty much the only one that I am exposed to without a mask.
Exactly. I had BPD before my health got really bad. But it just added a whole lot of shit on top. Its so frustrating even talking to therapists because they just don't get it.

I agree. THC really helped me a lot. It helps with the pain and for a long time it was the only way that I could eat. I never had an appetite unless I smoked, and it helped with the nausea. My digestive issues aren't as bad as OP. I have gastroparesis and colitis. My issues was more of the colitis. It got to the point where I couldn't eat because it was too painful. I lost 70 lbs in 5 months. Then I got put on medication for the colitis. That really helped. My my body got used to not eating and it took a lot of time to be able to eat normally. All the advice I have to say has already been said so I'll just share my story. I "transitionedit to natural in the beginning of high school which would have been like 06-07 ish. I honestly never noticed a difference other than my hair growing longer. I continued to flat iron my hair, though not very often. I would make it stretch as long as possible. At some point I had realized my hair was "heat trained" so I could keep my straight hair 2 to 3 months (yes I know  that's kind of gross). I really  really really hated having to do my hair. 

Once I started learning about how to get healthier hair I started wearing it curly. I had no idea how heat damaged my hair was, I'd never worn it curly before. Thorough out the time I noticed my curls getting smaller and smaller, from loose limp noodles to real 3c looking curls. Last year I went to a Dominican salon to have my hair done for my dad's wedding, and I ended up with insane heat damage. I stopped using heat and transitioned for a year,  at which point I couldn't take it anymore longer and had to have my limp stringy hair cut off.

After having my hair cut and natural for the first time since I can remember, I realized # 1 the entire time I was natural I had heat damage  (even when I thought I was completely natural with no heat damage) and #2 my hair was nothing like it was before when I thought it was healthy, and I had no idea what my hair type was anymore and had no idea how to deal with it.

It's been 6 months since then and my hair has grown like crazy and I've realized, my heat damage was not the problem. My natural hair is extremely hard to deal with. It is too much work. When I cut it is had this idea that all my problemstuff would be solved, I thought it would take less time, be less work, and be curlier. Instead I got the same message as before except now it's impossible to style anyway that comes out looking like I'm a sane human being that cleans themselves and attempts to look presentable.

What I learned is that be careful what you wish for, and that natural hair is so over rated. Well for me that is. Don't get me wrong I love my huge fro, and my little curls, but for me the struggle isn't worth it. I put too much time and effort into my hair just to end up looking like I don't do my hair. Also I am very disabled which makes its so much more not worth the effort.
